content.body:
When the 232 was introduced, it was the most sophisticated wheeled vehicle in the world, with 8-wheel-drive and 8 wheel steering, fully independent suspension and a rear-facing driver for quick reverse escapes. They had exceptional off-road handling capabilities, and were widely used for both long-range reconnaissance and as command vehicles. The characteristic bedframe antenna atop the 232 was for the Funkenwagen (Radio) model, and had a complicated mounting allowing the turret to turn freely.
The 232 was a successful vehicle, and the system proved its versatility in the later adoption of a number of variants, among them one with the short 75mm cannon originally found on the Pz.IVd and later the famed Puma Tank Destroyer with a long-barreled high velocity 50mm gun. Its basic design, an 8 wheel mobile armoured car with a light rapid firing gun mounted in a turret; is the same kind of specification of most modern light infantry combat vehicles worldwide today.
Control Variations: crew 2 no view slit.
The 232 remains an exceptionally mobile vehicle in Battleground Europe, although its top heavy nature makes it a little hard to handle (careful on the curves and crossing steep slopes) and it can be rolled easily. Its speed, even cross country; means that a hard-pressed town can be reinforced with swarms of 232s from undepleted rear or forward bases even two or three towns distant. Despite its light armor, it can be infuriatingly hard to kill because so much of it is empty space inside. Enemies can pump round after round of AP into it, but if they do not happen to hit a crewman, engine, fuel or ammunition storage ... they'll not manage to kill it easily.
When using the 232 in its recon role, remember to turn slightly to the right as you stop to view a forward subject ... the antenna post can block the commander's view when at full magnification. The suspension on the 232 is excellent, firing on the move while at top-speed even moving cross country is quite effective.
